sources.entry: School of SRE: Curriculum for onboarding non-traditional hires and new grads

summary.name: School of SRE
summary.one_liner: An open source curriculum from LinkedIn for teaching foundational site reliability engineering (SRE) skills to new graduates and non-traditional hires.
use_cases: Learning the foundations of site reliability engineering
Onboarding new graduate engineers into an SRE role
Preparing for an entry-level SRE job
Training non-traditional hires for SRE work
Finding reference material for further SRE study
summary.what_it_does: The page describes School of SRE, a course structured into Level 101 and Level 102 modules that focuses on foundational SRE skills. Each module includes real-life examples and references for further learning. The material covers how SREs translate business requirements into SLAs for system components, monitor adherence, and re-architect or scale systems to avoid breaches. LinkedIn says it uses the curriculum to onboard its own new hires and has open sourced the content so other organizations and aspiring engineers can use and contribute to it. The page does not list specific lesson topics beyond the two levels.
notable: Created by LinkedIn's Site Engineering team and open sourced for other organizations
Structured as Level 101 and Level 102 modules with references in each module
Community contributions welcomed via a contributing guide
caveats: Page lists only two levels and does not detail the individual lesson topics
Content is described as a starting point that the community is expected to refine and expand
